identification: Seven tall conical uranium (vaseline) glass goblets/vases with gold-fleck (aventurine) knop stems on clear-ish uranium feet, plus three uranium coupes with spiral-ribbed bowls, pink gold-fleck dolphin stems and swirl-ribbed feet. Venetian/Murano, Salviati style, early to mid 20th century. Re-opened all 3 photos at full size (very small source images, about 350x263 and 200x260 px): no signatures, labels or etched marks visible, so maker is not confirmed. Photos 2 and 3 are UV-glow shots (strong green glow). The 7 goblets do NOT have dolphin stems, only the 3 coupes do, so the dolphin-stem comparables apply to 3 of the 10 pieces.

viewing_check: Armitage estimate 100-150, current bid $80 (checked 9 Nov 2026), buyer's premium 22%, closes 11 Nov about 2:48 pm. Terapeak US shows single Salviati dolphin stem goblets/glasses selling A$65-182 each over the last 3 years (most A$80-180, typical about A$105-140), whole sets A$800-900 for 5-8; AU Terapeak has almost nothing (0 rows for 'murano dolphin coupe', 4 rows for 'salviati dolphin', none goblets); GB A$40-250. Prices are 2023 to 2026, mostly 2025-2026, flat to slightly firm. Those listings are mostly sellers labelling pieces Salviati, and many are US market with higher postage-inclusive pricing; Andy's lot is unmarked so it would sell as 'Murano/Venetian, attributed'. Auction results (Lawsons, LiveAuctioneers, Invaluable, Carter's) gave no usable dolphin-stem glass sold prices. Check in hand: chips on the dolphin fins and rims, fins are the usual breakage, cracks at the join, UV glow, marks under the feet. At about $80 hammer the three dolphin coupes alone look worth roughly A$100-130 each on US-sourced eBay evidence, so a hammer up to the estimate looks reasonable to Andy as a buyer, the 7 plain-stem goblets are the unknown.
